messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Take atorvastatin tablet once daily with or without food. Many people ask when to take atorvastatin morning or night? It can be taken any time of the day, but try and take it at the same time each day.
Take the liquid medicine on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before a meal or 2 hours after a meal. Shake the oral suspension (liquid). Measure a dose with the supplied measuring device (not a kitchen spoon).
Take atorvastatin exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets. Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Do not change your dose or stop taking any of your medications without your doctor's advice.
It may take up to 2 weeks before your cholesterol levels improve, and you may need frequent blood tests. Even if you have no symptoms, tests can help your doctor determine if this medicine is effective.
Your treatment may also include diet, exercise, weight control, and blood tests.
Store at room temperature away from moisture, heat, and light.
Throw away in the trash any unused liquid 60 days after opening the bottle.
Triples: [["atorvastatin", "administered via", "tablet"], ["atorvastatin", "can be taken with", "food"], ["atorvastatin", "can be taken without", "food"], ["atorvastatin", "has alternative form", "oral suspension"], ["atorvastatin", "should be taken on empty stomach", "at least 1 hour before a meal"], ["atorvastatin", "should be taken on empty stomach", "at least 2 hours after a meal"], ["atorvastatin", "requires shaking", "before use"], ["atorvastatin", "requires precise dosing", "using supplied measuring device"], ["atorvastatin", "must be taken as prescribed", "by doctor"], ["atorvastatin", "requires reading of", "prescription label"], ["atorvastatin", "requires reading of", "medication guides"], ["atorvastatin", "may require dose adjustment", "by doctor"], ["atorvastatin", "should not be changed or stopped", "without doctor's advice"], ["atorvastatin", "has delayed effect", "up to 2 weeks"], ["atorvastatin", "requires monitoring of", "cholesterol levels"], ["atorvastatin", "has treatment component", "diet"], ["atorvastatin", "has treatment component", "exercise"], ["atorvastatin", "has treatment component", "weight control"], ["atorvastatin", "has treatment component", "blood tests"], ["atorvastatin", "has storage instruction", "store at room temperature away from moisture, heat, and light"], ["atorvastatin", "has disposal instruction", "throw away unused liquid 60 days after opening"]]
Relations: ["administered via", "can be taken with", "can be taken without", "has alternative form", "has delayed effect", "has disposal instruction", "has storage instruction", "has treatment component", "may require dose adjustment", "must be taken as prescribed", "requires monitoring of", "requires precise dosing", "requires reading of", "requires shaking", "should be taken on empty stomach", "should not be changed or stopped"]
Answer:

completion:
administered via: The subject drug is delivered or administered through the specified route or physical form.
can be taken with: The subject drug can be consumed in conjunction with the specified food or meal.
can be taken without: The subject drug can be consumed without the specified food or meal.
has alternative form: The subject drug is available in a different pharmaceutical form than the primary one specified.
has delayed effect: The therapeutic effect of the subject drug may not be observed for the duration specified.
has disposal instruction: Unused or expired form of the subject drug should be disposed of according to the specified instructions.
has storage instruction: The subject drug should be stored under the specified conditions to maintain efficacy and safety.
has treatment component: The subject drug's treatment regimen includes the specified medical or lifestyle intervention.
may require dose adjustment: The dosage of the subject drug might need to be modified by a healthcare professional based on patient response or condition.
must be taken as prescribed: The subject drug should be consumed exactly as directed by a healthcare provider.
requires monitoring of: The subject drug's effectiveness or safety requires regular assessment of the specified medical parameter.
requires precise dosing: The subject drug must be administered in the exact amount specified using the designated measuring device.
requires reading of: The subject drug's correct use requires the patient to read and follow the specified informational materials.
requires shaking: The subject drug must be shaken before use to ensure uniformity of the formulation.
should be taken on empty stomach: The subject drug should be taken when the stomach is empty, either at least one hour before a meal or at least two hours after a meal.
should not be changed or stopped: The subject drug should not have its dosage or use altered without explicit guidance from a healthcare provider.
